card.name: Overdose treatment and swallowing-whole instructions
card.fires_on: Single words in dosing text that come right after a sentence about overdose or tablet handling, such as "Treatment" of overdose, "swallowed" whole, or "after" a number of days when resuming a drug.

modes.label: Overdose treatment
modes.description: The word "Treatment" or "treatment" opening a statement about managing overdose, after a line saying there is no antidote.
modes.example: There is no specific antidote for overdose with SYMTUZA.<< Treatment>> of overdose with SYMTUZA consists

modes.label: Swallowed whole
modes.description: The word "swallowed" in an instruction that tablets must not be crushed, cut or chewed.
modes.example: Tablets should not be crushed, cut, or chewed; they should be<< swallowed>> whole.

modes.label: Resume after a period
modes.description: The word "after" or "continuing" in instructions on when to resume a drug after recovery from a side effect.
modes.example: If recovered<< after>> 7 days, resume IWILFIN

card.plain: It marks the key word in stock dosing sentences about overdose care, swallowing tablets whole, and when to restart a drug.
